Rev C mechanics register CALC-C01…C18 lives on M-106 / M-107 / M-108. CALC-C01 is historical (Rev B FAIL) — it is why the axis was redesigned.
AUTOMATED CHECKS RUN ON EVERY REGENERATION
✓ Table narrower than the inner span, and way projection greater than zero.
✓ Way rebate does not cut through the side panel.
✓ Drum shorter than the inner span; drum length still the 21-disc pack.
✓ Lift travel covers the full thickness range.
✓ Stretchers do not intersect the table envelope, drum, or motor (validate_mechanics).
✓ Vertical ways cover table travel; both Acme screws sit on the drum centerline.
✓ Every part and hardware ID named in a build step exists in the registry.
✓ Every fabricated part is used by at least one build step.
✓ Every QC gate referenced by a step exists in the inspection plan.
Solid sliding table, no conveyor, adjustable idler,
Dual-end lift, UHMW ways, hold-downs, floating bearing,
Fabrication model: part/joint IDs, housed stretchers,
way rebate so table fits, derived geometry, JSON/CSV
named hole patterns; idler axial pad (not YZ slots)
Master build guide book: G-001…G-004 design basis, E-101
ballooned explosion, ST-01…ST-14 step sheets with parts
Mechanics: vertical captured ways, stretcher stations
clear of the table, both Acme screws on the drum CL,
P-017 shoes / P-018 thrust / P-019 home dog, Planforge
Precision rebuild. Rev B's ¾″ shaft failed its own
accuracy spec at 4.25 lbf (CALC-C01), and one 0.003″
figure was being used for two different quantities. Rev
C: 1¼″ shaft + structural aluminium shell (21× stiffer),
adjustable gib, parallelism micro-adjust plate, bearings
specified by required dynamic capacity, spec split into
ALN-01 and TV-01, frame through-bolted, 18-step build
with an Option B drum, McMaster procurement register.
